records.real_world_identity_notes: The PMR telemetry name maps to Porsche's 996-generation 911 GT3 RSR used for the 2004 and 2005 racing seasons. This is the competition RSR, not the road-going 996 GT3 RS, the earlier 996 GT3 R/RS, or the later 997 GT3 RSR. The exact race-year sub-configuration is not supplied by the PMR observation, so 2004-2005 is retained as the model-family boundary.
records.confidence_basis: Contemporary 2004 Alex Job Racing material names the 2004 Porsche 911 GT3 RSR and supplies its race specification. Stuttcars independently scopes the 996 RSR to the 2004-2005 seasons and identifies the internal generation as 996. The PMR attachment supplies the matching telemetry name and N-GT class; it is used only to connect the observation to the real-car identity, not to establish real-car technique.

records.specification_basis: Contemporary team data and Porsche's technical summary both specify six forward gears. The 2004 team specification says dog type, straight-cut transmission; Porsche independently calls it a sequential jaw-type gearbox. The period Alex Job Racing photograph is captioned as showing the sequential gear shift, the specification names an in-line shift mechanism, and the later onboard description identifies a push-pull cockpit lever. No source supports steering-wheel paddles for this target. Both sources explicitly describe a sequential gearbox; the team source also identifies the in-line shift mechanism. The period specification documents sensor-controlled traction interruption, and the model history explicitly says the ignition cut enables shifts at full throttle. The documented sensor-controlled traction interruption is an automatic power cut associated with the shift mechanism; the independent description calls it ignition cut. Manual blip is a downshift action in this data model; no upshift-blip procedure is being asserted. Automatic blip is a downshift action in this data model; the documented upshift system is interruption/cut, not a blip. Throttle lift is recorded as an upshift action in this data model; no separate downshift-lift claim is made. The documented interruption is an upshift function; no downshift cut is established. The clear cockpit photograph shows fixed hand grips around a central button/control face rather than a continuous circular band. Under the data-model definition this is gt-formula. The wheel is a fixed-grip gt-formula control-face design; open_top is therefore not-applicable under the schema rather than a round/d-shaped rim yes/no property. The photograph nevertheless visibly shows the upper rim opening. The wheel face in the clear photograph contains controls but no display; the contemporary team specification places the MoTeC display in the electrical/dashboard system behind the wheel. The full-width photograph shows no light array on the wheel; the visible light strip is on the dashboard behind it. This is limited to the photographed restored configuration and does not claim that no 996 RSR ever used a different wheel. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip.
